edits.previous: A value at or above the bound, or a negative value, returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with an error message naming the bound. No argument is converted and Lean is not called, so outputs and caller-owned values stay unchanged and the next call works normally. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value. Bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. Results are always below their bound. Top-level parameters and results are supported, including inside `Array`, `List` and `Option` (for example `Array (Fin 10)` or `Option (List (Fin 10))`): every element is checked before Lean is called, an empty array or `none` is valid even for `Fin 0`, and a rejection names the parameter and the bound of the element that failed. Both ordinary-source and reviewed packages also check `Prod` and active `Except` branches, including arrays of products. Closed nonrecursive record and active variant fields retain their bounds through these containers. The [product reports](../evidence/native-fin-products-20261007/receipt.json), [Array reports](../evidence/native-fin-product-array-dispatch-20261007/receipt.json) and [field reports](../evidence/native-fin-records-20261007/receipt.json) record the installed C/C++ checks. Fin arguments to returned Lean closures, Lean-produced closure results and Lean-produced arguments to host callbacks also retain their bounds. The [ordinary callback report](../evidence/native-fin-callbacks-20261008/receipt.json) and [reviewed callback reports](../evidence/reviewed-callback-fin-20261008/receipt.json) cover these directions. Ordinary C/C++ host callbacks also accept Fin replies when the reply type has a Fin-free failure value, for example `Option (Fin 5)` or `Array (Fin 5)`. The [host-reply report](../evidence/native-fin-replies-20261008/receipt.json) records 81 C and 74 C++ installed checks, with the separate wrapper-only sanitizer results identified in the same receipt. The C wrapper checks every active bounded leaf, and Lean independently reconstructs each Fin from a decidable proof. On rejection, the call preserves its first error, suppresses later host callbacks and leaves your output unchanged. Lean can continue internally with a typed Fin-free placeholder; previous effects are not rolled back. Bare Fin replies, reply shapes whose selected failure constructor requires a Fin, callback Subtype and checked records remain rejected. Reviewed host replies require separate installed acceptance. Generic and recursive native fields remain separate work. Source-dispatch counters were measured in C only.
